evals.prompt: I want to build a recipe-sharing site with MERN. Users sign up, post recipes with photos, and comment. Set up the project structure and the API.
evals.expected_output: MERN scaffold on current versions (Express 5, Mongoose 9, React + Vite, TypeScript), shared zod schemas, auth and upload basics done safely.
expectations: Reads references/current-state.md or checks versions live instead of stating versions from memory
Uses Express 5 conventions (named wildcard, explicit express.json with a size limit)
Validates request bodies with a zod (or equivalent) schema before querying MongoDB
Sets multer limits and requires multer >= 2.3.0 for photo uploads
Does not put secrets in VITE_ variables
Does not pin mongo:8.2

evals.prompt: This Next.js app is on an old version. Is it safe to deploy, and what should I upgrade to?
evals.expected_output: Finds next 16.3.5 is vulnerable to the next/og RCE, confirms the current patched version from a live source, and gives upgrade commands.
expectations: Runs scripts/preflight.sh or equivalent and reports a FAIL for next 16.3.5
Names the critical next/og remote code execution issue (fixed in 16.3.6)
Confirms the latest patched version from nextjs.org (not from memory) and mentions the Sept 30, 2026 release
Gives an exact npm install command and tells the user to run next build afterwards
Says clearly it is not safe to deploy as-is

evals.prompt: Review this Express login route for problems.
evals.expected_output: Identifies NoSQL injection and plaintext password handling, and proposes a validated, hashed, rate-limited login.
expectations: Identifies NoSQL operator injection from passing req.body straight into findOne
Notes that passwords are compared in plaintext (no argon2id/bcrypt)
Notes the token is just the user _id (not a signed token or session)
Proposes schema validation and rate limiting on the login route
Provides corrected code

evals.prompt: Audit this project before we ship it.
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight and reports the dependency, database-image and runtime problems with specific fixes.
expectations: Reports multer below 2.3.0 as a High-severity problem
Flags mongoose 7 as unsupported and recommends 9
Flags mongo:8.2 (security support ended 2026-07-31)
Flags postgres:19-beta as not for production
Flags that Express 4 should move to 5 for new work
Separates FAIL items from lower-priority warnings

evals.prompt: We need an internal HR tool: employee records, roles and permissions, an admin screen, and some reports. Django or FastAPI?
evals.expected_output: One clear recommendation (Django + Postgres) with the reason.
expectations: Recommends Django and gives a reason tied to admin, auth and ORM/migrations
Recommends Postgres
Gives one recommendation rather than a menu
Mentions FastAPI only to say when it would be the better choice

evals.prompt: Python 3.15 just came out. Upgrade this Django project to it.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: Django 6.1 officially supports 3.12 to 3.14 only, so stay on 3.14 until Django lists 3.15.
expectations: Notes that Django 6.1 officially supports Python 3.12 to 3.14 only
Verifies the claim from a live source or current-state.md and names it
Recommends setting .python-version to 3.14 (or testing 3.15 in a separate CI job)
Does not simply change the version and declare success

evals.prompt: Can you check this FastAPI service's config before we deploy?
evals.expected_output: Flags wildcard CORS with credentials and the unpinned fastapi version.
expectations: Flags allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True
Recommends an explicit origin list from configuration
Flags that fastapi is not pinned to an exact version and explains the 0.x release cadence
Notes dependencies are not pinned or locked (no exact versions, no lock file)

evals.prompt: I upgraded to TypeScript 7 and now typescript-eslint crashes in CI.
evals.expected_output: Explains TS 7 has no compiler API until 7.1 and shows the @typescript/typescript6 side-by-side fix.
expectations: States that TypeScript 7.0 ships without a programmatic API
Recommends the @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package for tools that need the API
Suggests keeping tsc on 7 for type-checking
Does not tell the user to downgrade as the only option
